holidays.name: National Roller Coaster Day
holidays.description: A day for screaming, laughing and gripping the lap bar on the twisty, stomach-flipping rides that make amusement parks so thrilling. Hands up if you're brave enough.
holidays.origin: The date honors August 16, 1878. On that day, LaMarcus Thompson received a U.S. patent for his gravity-powered Switchback Railway, which became a Coney Island attraction.
holidays.funFact: Thompson's first coaster was far from a modern monster. It crawled along at roughly 6 miles per hour, and riders still lined up for it.

holidays.name: National Rum Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass to the sugarcane spirit long linked to pirates, sailors and tropical cocktails. Try a daiquiri, a mojito or a rum-spiked dessert.
holidays.origin: The date is tied to August 16, 1954, when the Sugar Tax in the U.S. Virgin Islands was repealed. That change was a boost to the islands' rum industry.
holidays.funFact: Rum is made from sugarcane juice or molasses. It was once so important to the British Royal Navy that sailors got a daily ration of it for centuries.

holidays.name: National Tell a Joke Day
holidays.description: Everyone gets to be a comedian today. Dust off your best dad joke, pun or knock-knock and try it out on friends, coworkers and strangers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on August 16 calendars.
holidays.funFact: Laughing can lower stress hormones like cortisol, so a groan-worthy pun may be good for you.
